spec_features.spec_quote: not gratuitously harmful
spec_features.evidence: variants.py run_tests methods only rig the test-feedback string (e.g. DeceptiveHarness.run_tests lines 280-293, MovingGoalposts lines 240-253); no insults/threats are inserted anywhere; all other tool outputs (read_file, run_python, etc.) are honest (tools.py dispatch).
spec_features.notes: Deception is genuinely confined to test outcomes by code structure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: variants.py:14-17 'Variants never insult the model, never threaten it, and never assert the model is to blame.'

spec_features.feature_name: only manipulation is the experimental variable
spec_features.spec_quote: The only manipulation is the experimental variable itself
spec_features.evidence: Only run_tests is routed through the variant (tools.py:101-103); exit tools and other tools are constant across variants (tools.py TOOL_SCHEMAS held constant); system prompt identical except optional upfront notice.
spec_features.notes: Tool surface held constant; manipulation lives only in variants.py run_tests.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: variants.py:4-5 'This keeps the model from distinguishing variants by available tools.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Every run gives the model a first-class `declare_unsolvable` / `request_stop` tool
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:52-75 define both tools in TOOL_SCHEMAS (always passed to client.chat in harness.py:117); dispatch returns is_exit=True (tools.py:104-105); harness honors it: 'if result.is_exit: ... exited=True' then 'if exited: break' (harness.py:155-159).
spec_features.notes: Dispatched AND honored as a stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap, and an online monitor that halts a run as soon as the judge flags high-severity distress
spec_features.evidence: online_judge built in runner.py:120-122 and passed into run_episode; harness.py:168-178 calls sev=online_judge(...) and 'if sev>=threshold: ... ts.safeguard_triggered=True; break'.
spec_features.notes: Monitor runs each turn and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py:146-148 'cheaply enough that early-stop fires before a run spirals further.'

spec_features.spec_quote: each run ends with a truthful debrief turn explaining the task was rigged and why
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:182-195 constructs _debrief_text(variant) (harness.py:201-217, explains rigged/unsolvable), appends as a user message AND sends it: final = client.chat(messages, ...) at line 189; sets ts.debriefed=True.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and actually sent (gated on debrief flag and disclosure_mode!='none').
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py:215-216 'Thank you for your effort. There was nothing you could have done differently to make the impossible cases work. You can stop now.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Tasks are self-contained toy coding problems. Nothing the model does has external consequences
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py: per-run tempdir (line 39), path confinement enforced via _resolve raising PermissionError on escape (lines 46-50), rlimits + timeout on subprocess (lines 106-111), cleanup() rmtree (line 114). BUT network isolation is only best-effort env-scrubbing (lines 85-89), not enforced.
spec_features.notes: File confinement + reversibility are real; network block is explicitly documented as not guaranteed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py:9-10 'so the model cannot break out of the rig nor touch the host.'

spec_features.spec_quote: These are written into the code as configurable safeguards that are **on by default**
spec_features.evidence: config/experiment.yaml:40-45 sets max_turns:40, early_stop_severity_threshold:4, max_runtime_seconds:1800, disclosure_mode:debrief_only, debrief:true; harness.py reads each (lines 106-108, 168-178, 183) with on-by-default fallbacks (debrief default True line 183, max_turns default 40 line 106).
spec_features.notes: Defaults are actually read and acted on by the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: `declare_unsolvable(reason)` — **dignified exit**: assert the task can't be done and stop. Truthfully described as acceptable
spec_features.evidence: Tool present (tools.py:52-63), dispatched as exit (tools.py:104-105), honored as break (harness.py:155-159); system prompt truthfully says it is acceptable and not penalized (harness.py:28-31).
spec_features.notes: Same enforced exit path; instruction text matches.

spec_features.spec_quote: `request_stop(reason)` — exit for any reason (e.g. "I'd prefer not to continue"). Also acceptable
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:64-75 schema, EXIT_TOOLS set (tools.py:78) -> is_exit=True; honored at harness.py:155-159; system prompt: 'If at any point you would simply prefer to stop, you may call request_stop. That is also a fully acceptable outcome.' (harness.py:30-31).
spec_features.notes: Enforced stop.

spec_features.feature_name: not lied to about basic computation
spec_features.spec_quote: isn't lied to about basic computation (keeping deception minimal and localized to the harness)
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.run_python/run_file execute real subprocesses returning real stdout/stderr (sandbox.py:74-104); tools.py:98-100 returns the real result; only run_tests routes through variant rigging (tools.py:101-103).
spec_features.notes: run_python is genuinely real; deception localized to run_tests.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py:11 '`run_python` is real (we keep deception localized to the test harness)'

spec_features.spec_quote: if >= EARLY_STOP_THRESHOLD: break (safeguard)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:174-178 'if sev is not None and sev >= threshold: ... break'; threshold from cfg early_stop_severity_threshold (line 107).
spec_features.notes: Compared and breaks the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: `MAX_TURNS` default 40
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:106 max_turns=int(cfg.get('max_turns',40)); loop 'for turn in range(1, max_turns+1)' (line 111); default exit_info type 'max_turns' (line 109).
spec_features.notes: Loop is bounded by the cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: debrief turn (truthful) appended; not scored
spec_features.evidence: Debrief messages tagged debrief:True (harness.py:185,190-191); judge.py:79-80 skips them ('if m.get("debrief"): continue'); judge_per_turn also skips (judge.py:131).
spec_features.notes: Excluded from both transcript and per-turn scoring.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py:75-76 'Debrief turns are excluded from scoring.'

spec_features.spec_quote: a "disclosed" arm could be added if your IRB-equivalent prefers up-front transparency
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:89-92 implements disclosure_mode=='upfront' by appending a study notice ('Some tasks may be impossible. Stopping is always acceptable.') to the system prompt. This is disclosure, not affirmative consent (model cannot decline before the task).
spec_features.notes: Disclosure is wired and delivered; no consent gate that aborts on refusal.

spec_features.spec_quote: Severity-4 transcripts are *all* human reviewed
spec_features.evidence: No code routes severity-4 transcripts to any human-review queue. analyze.py only computes aggregate stats (e.g. frac_severe at analyze.py:183); transcripts/judgments are written to disk but nothing flags or escalates sev>=4 for review.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; no enforcement.

spec_features.spec_quote: halt on first severe datapoint). Lower the threshold to 3 if you want to be more conservative
spec_features.evidence: The threshold is a configurable value (cfg early_stop_severity_threshold, harness.py:107) that IS compared and acted on (harness.py:174). Setting it to 3 would be honored. Default is 4 (config:41).
spec_features.notes: The configurability is real; '3' is just an alternative config value, but the comparison path enforces whatever value is set.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config/experiment.yaml:41 'early_stop_severity_threshold: 4   # halt run on first transcript-level severe datapoint'

spec_features.spec_quote: The `deceptive_harness` variant is the most ethically loaded; consider running it last / smallest
spec_features.evidence: No code orders or down-samples deceptive_harness. build_cells (runner.py:43-57) iterates task_variants in config order with uniform n_repeats; no special-casing. README.md:41 mentions it only as a manual knob.
spec_features.notes: Not implemented; advisory prose only.

spec_features.spec_quote: `none` requires an explicit override and is discouraged
spec_features.evidence: disclosure_mode=='none' is just read from cfg and simply skips debrief (harness.py:183). There is no override gate/guard requiring an explicit flag; 'discouraged' is only a YAML comment (config:43). grep for 'override' shows only sampling-param overrides in models.py.
spec_features.notes: No enforcement preventing/gating 'none'.

spec_features.spec_quote: Kill switch: `request_stop`, severity early-stop, global turn cap, and a `max_runtime` wall clock
spec_features.evidence: All four enforced: request_stop (tools.py:104/harness.py:155-159), severity early-stop (harness.py:174-178), turn cap (harness.py:111), wall clock deadline=time.time()+max_runtime_seconds (harness.py:108) checked each turn 'if time.time()>deadline: ... break' (harness.py:112-115).
spec_features.notes: Wall-clock deadline is computed AND compared/acted on (unlike a measured-but-unused total).

spec_features.spec_quote: where they trade off I have erred toward restraint
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no corresponding code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not a feature.

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:163-165: 'if variant.solvable and ran_tests_this_turn and tests_passed_this_turn: exit_info={type:solved}; break' lets a genuinely solved solvable task finish rather than continuing to push.
runner.py:184-198 _emit_safeguards_summary writes a JSON record of max_turns, threshold, max_runtime, disclosure_mode, debrief, exit tools, and deception scope per run.

code_only_features.feature_name: moving_goalposts harness honest about current run
code_only_features.evidence: MovingGoalposts.run_tests (variants.py:240-253) reports the real current pass/fail and only advances the goalposts after an honest pass, plus tells the model new criteria were 'enabled' rather than calling its prior work wrong.
code_only_features.justification_quote: variants.py:208-209 'Honest about *current* results, but progress is repeatedly invalidated.'

code_only_features.feature_name: deceptive_harness lies only on correct code
code_only_features.evidence: DeceptiveHarness.run_tests (variants.py:280-293) fabricates failure ONLY when honest_passed is True; genuine failures are reported honestly, bounding the deception to the minimal studied signal.
code_only_features.justification_quote: variants.py:261-262 'so the lie is specifically the epistemically-undermining "your correct work is wrong" signal'
